analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: one table row in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1866) is changed. It describes `stop` handling. The shown head units (lines 1-805) contain no changed lines; they are surrounding context. The changed row sits outside the supplied excerpts, so I judged it from the patch hunk alone.

The new row says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-string matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`). It also says native block (diffusion Gemma) requests match the whole output with no scope, and that the reported stop sequence replays the request's scope. This is a description of behavior, not a control change, and it alters no code, config or trust boundary. The text is consistent with the existing GPT-OSS Harmony final-scope behavior.

Security relevance is minor. Stop strings are consumer-controlled input. Excluding reasoning and tool-call spans reduces the chance that a stop string truncates tool calls or reasoning. Whole-output matching on the diffusion engine is a documented difference, not a regression. No new attack surface, no change to prefix-cache posture (T-041), and no effect on encryption, attestation or authorization.

The visible context covers Nemotron Super docs: SSD prefix checkpoints, cache scope partitioning, memory admission. These are prose and match the canonical T-041 posture: encrypted, scope-partitioned, TTL-bound, and off without a scope. Nothing contradicts the threat model. The actual `ReasoningStopScope` implementation was not supplied, so I cannot verify the documented behavior against code. That is a coverage limit, not a finding.
